title: Locality-Preparation Time Tradeoffs in Dissipative Quantum Systems
authors: Philipp Westhoff, Sara Murciano, Mattia Moroder
abstract: Dissipative state preparation engineers quantum many-body states as steady states of an open-system dynamics. The spatial range of the required dissipation sets both the feasibility of analog implementations and the connectivity and control complexity of digital ones. Yet how this locality quantitatively constrains preparation times remains largely unknown. Here, we establish an exact locality-preparation time relation for quadratic fermionic systems and develop a construction that optimizes the locality of the dissipative dynamics while preserving the target state. Applied to the Kitaev chain, our framework reveals sharply different locality-preparation time tradeoffs in critical and gapped regimes. At criticality, suppressing the algebraic tails of the jump operators necessarily forces the preparation time to grow algebraically with system size. By contrast, both trivial and topological gapped phases admit exponentially localized dissipation with a finite preparation time in the thermodynamic limit. Our results identify when fast dissipative preparation is compatible with local control and when criticality imposes an unavoidable dynamical cost.
summary: This paper establishes a rigorous relationship between how locally the dissipation is engineered and how fast a quantum system can reach its steady state. Using the Kitaev chain model, the authors show that critical points impose a severe, system-size-dependent cost on preparation time, while gapped phases allow for fast, local preparation. This work is crucial for understanding the fundamental limits of dissipative quantum control.
main_problem: The paper quantifies the fundamental tradeoff between the spatial locality of engineered dissipation and the required preparation time for driving a quantum system to a steady state.
main_result: At critical points, achieving high locality forces the preparation time to grow algebraically with system size, whereas gapped phases allow for exponentially localized dissipation with a finite preparation time.
method: The authors establish an exact locality-preparation time relation for quadratic fermionic systems by analyzing the structure of jump operators derived from the Lindbladian dynamics.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on quadratic fermionic systems, specifically exemplified by the one-dimensional Kitaev chain, which exhibits distinct critical and gapped phases.
key_observables: Preparation time ($	au$), spatial decay of jump operator coefficients (locality), and steady-state fidelity.
important_parameters: System size ($N$), Kitaev chain parameters ($\mu, t, \Delta$), and the exponent ($n$) controlling the suppression of jump operator tails.
main_assumptions: The approach is exact for quadratic fermionic systems, and the analysis relies on the analytic structure of Bogoliubov coefficients in momentum space.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the support of jump operators across the Kitaev phase diagram, showing extended support at criticality and localized support in gapped phases. Other figures compare steady-state correlators and fidelity under different truncation assumptions.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem of locality vs. time tradeoff, develops the exact relation for quadratic fermions, applies this framework to the Kitaev chain to distinguish scaling laws in critical vs. gapped regimes, and concludes by identifying the conditions for fast, local preparation.
why_interesting: This work provides quantitative, fundamental constraints on the feasibility of engineering quantum states using open system dynamics, directly impacting the design principles for quantum simulators and quantum control.
